title: Tamil Shaivism and the Tevaram
hook: a wedding stopped by an old man waving a deed that says the groom is his slave: how Sundarar's first hymn began with an insult

segments.voice: Yesterday, Tamil Shaivism and the Tevaram: a sealed room at Chidambaram, palm leaves eaten by ants, and what this age needs, kept. Did you pass on something you were given in part? Day one thousand three hundred seventy-one.

The wedding is under way. The groom is a handsome young man named Arurar, the families are gathered, the rites have begun. Then an old Brahmin pushes through the crowd, holding up a palm-leaf deed. This young man, he announces, is my slave. His grandfather signed him over to me, him and all his line. The groom loses his temper. He calls the old man a madman and tears the deed to pieces. That insult, the story says, is how one of the Tevaram's three singers found his first word.
screen: `A WEDDING UNDER WAY.` → `AN OLD MAN WITH A DEED.` → `YOU MADMAN.`

segments.voice: The story is told in the Periya Puranam, in paraphrase. The old man isn't put off by the torn deed. That was only a copy, he says. The original is kept in his own town. So the whole wedding party follows him there, and before the village elders he produces the deed. They compare the handwriting with the grandfather's. It matches. The groom is bound. Then the old man leads them toward the temple, walks inside, and vanishes. It was Shiva. And Shiva speaks to the young man. You called me a madman. So sing of me, and begin with that word. The young man, known ever after as Sundarar, opens his first hymn with it. In paraphrase: madman, wearing the crescent moon in your hair. He calls Shiva the very name he shouted in anger, and turns it into praise. Turn that once. Shiva in this story doesn't wait for good manners. He takes the insult and hands it back as a first line. Turn it again. Look at the deed. In Tamil Shaivism devotees are called adiyar, the Lord's servants. Sundarar's whole calling begins with a document saying exactly that: he belongs to someone. The story says he spent his life singing from temple to temple, and the tradition remembers him with a second title as well, the Lord's friend. Servant and friend, in one man. Turn it once more. The wedding didn't happen. That's a hard ending for a bride, and the story doesn't hide it. Tomorrow, an older singer, and a king who summons him.
screen: `THE DEED IS REAL` · `THE OLD MAN WAS SHIVA` · `BEGIN WITH THAT WORD: MADMAN` · `SERVANT AND FRIEND`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: the word you shouted. Sit, and let the breath slow. Bring to mind something you said recently in frustration, a sharp word, aimed at a person, or at life, or at God. Don't scold yourself. Just hear it again, quietly. Then ask: is there any truth or longing hidden inside it? Let the word soften as you breathe. If you pray, you can offer that word back, the way Sundarar did, as the start of a prayer. The bell holds the time.
Tamil Shaivism and the Tevaram. Today, Sundarar, stopped at his own wedding by Shiva in disguise, whose first hymn begins with the insult he shouted: madman. Today's word.
screen: `TAMIL SHAIVISM AND THE TEVARAM — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: Tamil Shaivism and the Tevaram. Today, when you catch a sharp word on your tongue, see if it can be turned into something kinder before it lands. Day one thousand three hundred seventy-one.

howItsDone: Tamil Shaivas sing Sundarar's hymns as part of the Tevaram in temple worship, and his story is told from the Periya Puranam.

fork.reveal: he calls the old man a madman and tears the deed. it was only a copy, and later Shiva tells him to begin his first hymn with that very word.

trapdoor: what you thought: a hymn to God starts with polite praise.
what it means: Sundarar's first hymn starts with madman, the insult he shouted, because Shiva told him to.
what a scholar hears: a story about belonging, servant and friend at once, set at the head of a body of Tevaram hymns.

notes: Confirm the Periya Puranam sequence: the wedding at Puttur interrupted, the deed torn, 'only a copy', the original verified before the elders at Tiruvennainallur against the grandfather's hand, the old man vanishing into the temple, Shiva telling him to sing beginning with 'pittan' (madman).
First hymn 'Pitta pirai cudi' paraphrased as 'madman, wearing the crescent moon in your hair'; confirm.
'The Lord's friend' (Tambiran Tozhan) as Sundarar's title; and 'adiyar' glossed as the servant at the feet; confirm.
